title: What If the Mississippi River Changed Its Course?

scenes.text: What if the Mississippi River changed course? Engineers have fought that for seventy years.
A giant structure in Louisiana holds the split at seventy percent main river, thirty percent down the Atchafalaya.
Left alone, the Atchafalaya's share climbed from under ten percent in 1850 to about thirty percent by 1950.
In 1953 the Army Corps of Engineers warned the Mississippi would switch courses by 1990.
If it did, most of the flow would pour down the Atchafalaya, and the ports of New Orleans and Baton Rouge would lose their river.
In 1973 a flood nearly broke the structure. Rivers like this switch about every thousand years. This one is overdue.

description:
What if the Mississippi River changed course?
A control structure keeps about 70 percent of the flow in the main channel, but the Atchafalaya has been pulling harder for 170 years.
